title: Errors are caught and shown, never thrown at the console
note: Nothing throws, rejects or logs console.error; a failure is caught and shown in the page with a way to retry.
intent: An uncaught error is the cheapest evidence a build is broken, and a person who sees nothing happen has no way to know why. Catch at the edges where things can fail (a fetch, a parse, a storage read) and turn the failure into a message on the screen: what went wrong in words, and a retry or a way back. Handle promise rejections (await inside try/catch, or .catch) and never leave a console.error as the only signal. Guard what the data might not be: a missing field, an empty list, a number that is NaN. The page counts errors it saw (uncaught, rejected, console.error, failed resource loads) in state().ui.errors and keeps the last in ui.lastError.

check.note: Nothing on the page threw, rejected, called console.error or failed to load: state().ui.errors is 0.

port: Wrap each async action in one helper that catches, records the message in the store and renders it in a role="alert" region; components never need their own try/catch.
